name: Playwright
summary: Cross-browser automation for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with auto-waiting, isolated browser contexts and a built-in test runner for TypeScript.
strengths: Auto-waiting actions and web-first assertions remove most explicit waits.
A fresh browser context per test makes isolation cheap.
Trace viewer records DOM snapshots, network and console for every step.
Parallel workers and sharding are built into the TypeScript runner.
The same API covers browser and HTTP tests (APIRequestContext).
tradeoffs: WebKit is not the same as testing real Safari on macOS or iOS.
The richest runner features (fixtures, sharding, UI mode) are TypeScript-first; other languages rely on their own test runners.
No native mobile app support; mobile web is emulated.
